newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol freight charges system will be dropped.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol freight charges system will be dropped.

text.p: A unique system of handling charges paid by air freight shippers at Schiphol airport are to be phased out by January 1 next year, the Air Transport Association of the Netherlands (ATAN) said in a statement.

The trade body, which represents Netherlands-based air cargo carriers, said a compromise has been reached between its member companies and the Dutch association of air freight handling companies, NVVL.

The charges, known as zendingscosten, had been the focus of an independent study commissed to resolve a controversial debate about handling charges which had split the shipping, airline, freight forwarding and cargo handling sectors.
ATAM said that over the first six months of this year, all involved parties will implement a new system, which aims to cut the charges applied by around 50 percent.

The charges, estimated to cost shippers between 5 and 8 million guilders a year, have traditionally been levied at the leading Dutch airport by cargo handlers and forwarders for receiving air freight as it arrives at the airport for onward despatch.

ATAN said the aim is to gradually reduce the costs in the first part of this year, reduce them still further in the last six months of 1997 in anticipation of phasing the charge out once and for all from January 1 next year.
The zenidngscosten system has no equivalent at other European airports, and was perceived by Dutch shippers, and their trade organisation EVO, to be unfair.

The charges had evolved in the days when air freight needed to be prepared for carriage. Dutch shippers had argued that they had no place today when cargo arrives ready for shipment. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
